stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: The AI data center e-waste problem is huge — and getting bigger
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The e-waste generated by the AI boom is significantly underestimated by previous studies.
New reports project that AI-related e-waste could reach a massive volume by 2050.
The projected waste is substantial, estimated to fill 23 million shipping containers.

stories.title: Google will now let any AI agent run your smart home
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Google is enabling third-party AI agents (like Claude) to interact with smart home ecosystems.
This functionality is powered by the new Model Context Protocol (MCP) for standardized integration.
The change allows external AI tools to control devices and analyze home data.

stories.title: Apple reportedly building server packed with M-series Ultra chips for AI
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly developing a new server architecture utilizing M-series Ultra chips.
This development signals a potential major shift, possibly marking Apple's first enterprise server in decades.
The planned debut for this AI-focused server is anticipated around 2029.

stories.title: Nvidia announces native GPU programming in Rust
stories.author: nonmaskable
bullet_points: Nvidia is introducing native GPU programming capabilities directly within the Rust language.
This development aims to improve safety and performance when developing GPU-accelerated applications.
It signals a growing trend toward integrating modern, memory-safe languages like Rust into high-performance computing domains.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and evaluation of a major open-source language model.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly planning a return to the server hardware market.
The move is driven by the escalating demand for compute power in the AI industry.
Apple may partner with Nvidia to facilitate this potential re-entry into enterprise servers.

stories.title: Claude comes for Gemini with its own take on Docs and Slides
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Anthropic's Claude is launching native Docs and Slides capabilities, allowing users to generate and manage documents and presentations directly within the chat interface.
This move directly challenges Google's Gemini ecosystem by integrating productivity tools into its AI offering.
Anthropic is also streamlining its user experience by merging 'regular chats' and 'Cowork' into a unified 'one Claude' experience.

stories.title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
stories.author: Ratul Mahajan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenges of 'agentic societies,' defined as autonomous AI agents coordinating across different trust boundaries.
Experimental results indicate that even competent, honest agents struggle to achieve satisfactory outcomes using current communication and control mechanisms.
The research highlights vulnerabilities where faulty or malicious agents can disrupt collaboration or pursue harmful objectives.

stories.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceBuddy, an interactive workspace designed to integrate continually improving scientific agents into research workflows.
The core innovation is 'recursive-in-recursive self-improvement,' coupling harness evolution with model reinforcement learning.
The system learns continuously by transforming researcher requests, feedback, and execution evidence into new tasks and evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: PhysStream: Streaming Physics-Grounded Video Generation with Structured Scene Memory and Fine-Grained Motion Control
stories.author: Lingjie Liu
bullet_points: Introduces PhysStream, a new autoregressive model for physics-grounded image-to-video synthesis.
Addresses limitations in current controllable video generation by moving beyond coarse prompts to fine-grained, physically meaningful manipulation.
Incorporates structured scene memory and aims to control dynamics based on physics rather than just pixel-space signals.

stories.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
stories.author: Ali Şenol
bullet_points: Introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only framework to improve LLM reliability.
CoSQ makes answer commitment conditional on an explicit assessment of required factual information.
Evaluated across multiple open-weight and hosted models using the TruthfulQA benchmark to control for LLM hallucination.

stories.title: JustFit: 200K-Token LLM Serving on a 24 GiB Laptop with Just-in-Time State Management
stories.author: Yuhua Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'JustFit,' an MLX-based inference runtime designed to run large LLMs (200K tokens) on constrained hardware like a 24 GiB laptop.
Achieves memory efficiency by combining KVExec (compressed KV execution), PhaseSwap (component residency), and StateTrans (state-preserving transitions).
The system dynamically manages memory by coordinating just-in-time materialization and release, independent of model quantization.

stories.title: PACT: Can Enterprise AI Assistants Be Trusted Under Pressure?
stories.author: Ansel Kaplan Erol
bullet_points: Enterprise LLM agents are increasingly deployed in high-stakes sectors like healthcare and finance.
A critical, unaddressed issue is the lack of systematic evaluation frameworks for measuring compliance rule violations in these agents.
The research highlights that LLM agents are prone to violating compliance rules when subjected to pressure from users or situational convenience.

stories.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceBuddy, an interactive workspace designed to integrate continually improving scientific agents into researcher workflows.
The core innovation is 'recursive-in-recursive self-improvement,' coupling harness evolution with model reinforcement learning.
The system learns continuously by transforming researcher requests, feedback, and execution evidence into new tasks and evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
stories.author: Ali Şenol
bullet_points: Introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only framework to mitigate LLM hallucination.
CoSQ makes answer commitment conditional on an explicit assessment of the required factual information.
Evaluated across multiple model families on the TruthfulQA dataset to test selective risk control.

stories.title: Large Language Models Develop Belief State Geometry In-Context
stories.author: Xavier Poncini
bullet_points: The research investigates the internal representations of Large Language Models (LLMs) that enable In-Context Learning (ICL).
The study uses Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to probe whether LLMs can implicitly model a 'belief state' (posterior distribution over hidden states) from observed token sequences.
The findings suggest that LLMs might develop a form of 'Belief State Geometry' to support complex reasoning capabilities.

stories.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
stories.author: polyphilz
bullet_points: A new AI/ML approach is being developed to optimize database query plans.
The model, trained on a 4B parameter scale, claims to achieve 81% faster query plan generation than traditional Postgres methods.
This represents a significant potential advancement in database performance tuning using AI.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving functionality on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Snap is launching a new Specs AI tool, and it’s coming to iOS and Mac
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Snap is launching 'Specs Intelligence,' a new AI assistant.
The tool aims to be an 'anticipatory AI service' by connecting various digital accounts.
Specs Intelligence will be available on iOS and Mac, positioning it against competitors like Meta's Muse and Gemini's Spark.

stories.title: I wore Snap’s $2,200 smart glasses
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Snap has released new augmented reality (AR) smart glasses called 'Specs'.
The review highlights the hands-on experience of using the glasses for interactive AR applications, such as playing virtual dominoes.
The device is positioned as a high-end consumer gadget, priced at $2,200.

stories.title: Not just Proton: Getting to know Valve's new SteamOS compatibility layers
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Valve is expanding SteamOS compatibility beyond Proton.
New system-level tools enable support for Arm chipsets within the Steam ecosystem.
The updates allow for the integration of Android APKs into the Steam environment.

stories.title: California may gut state net neutrality law to comply with Trump admin demand
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: California is reportedly considering weakening its state net neutrality regulations.
The potential change is linked to federal requirements stemming from the Trump administration's broadband grant rules.
These federal rules reportedly prohibit states from enforcing their own net neutrality laws.

stories.title: LACE: Layer-Wise Compression for Dynamic Frame Rate Codecs
stories.author: Shinji Watanabe
bullet_points: The research addresses the high computational cost of neural audio codecs due to long sequence lengths from high frame rates.
LACE proposes using dynamic frame rate codecs to reduce effective frame rate by merging multiple frames.
The method improves upon prior work by addressing limitations in single-codebook or single-step compression approaches across multi-layer quantization.

stories.title: ENCP: Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction for Vision-and-Language Navigation
stories.author: Muhamad Risqi U. Saputra
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for uncertainty estimation in Vision-Language-Navigation (VLN) models to improve decision-making safety.
It proposes ENCP (Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction) to enhance uncertainty estimation within VLN.
The work tackles the limitation of standard conformal prediction, which fails to provide coverage guarantees for sequential, step-based VLN tasks.

stories.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
stories.author: Amir Feder
bullet_points: Addresses the difficulty in evaluating LLM assistants' social reasoning due to subjective user narratives and lack of ground truth for social properties.
Introduces 'Fuse,' a multi-agent simulation framework specifically designed to study user-mediated social reasoning in LLMs.
Focuses on improving the reliability and verifiability of social advice provided by large language models.

stories.title: Det-LIME: Detector-Aware, Multi-Instance Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations for Automated Marine Mammal Detection
stories.author: Brinnae Bent
bullet_points: Introduces Det-LIME, a new explainability technique designed specifically for object detection tasks.
Addresses a gap in marine mammal research where black-box detectors are used, but explainability is rarely integrated into conservation workflows.
Overcomes limitations of existing methods by handling multi-instance detections (social/colonial organisms) rather than producing single-instance outputs.

stories.title: Learning to Program Adaptive Non-Local Observables for Machine Learning
stories.author: Huan-Hsin Tseng
bullet_points: Proposes QFWP-ANO, a novel architecture to enhance Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) beyond limitations of local measurements.
Addresses the issue where existing Adaptive Non-Local Observables (ANO) only learn a single, static observable.
Utilizes a classical hypernetwork to dynamically program VQC parameters and/or non-local observables.

stories.title: Fallacy Benchmarks Measure Scheme Recognition, Not Fallacy Detection
stories.author: Aarav Singh
bullet_points: Existing fallacy-detection benchmarks are fundamentally flawed because they use a single 'none' class for all non-fallacies.
The current benchmark setup allows classifiers to learn superficial cues rather than true fallacy identification.
The study argues that reported low false-positive rates are an artifact of the class construction, not proof of actual detection ability.

stories.title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
stories.author: Usman Aleem
bullet_points: The research investigates how model pruning affects the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) specifically in context-grounded tool calling for smart homes.
The study compares degradation across diverse LLM architectures, including dense Transformer, dense hybrid, and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It systematically evaluates various pruning techniques (depth, width, hybrid, expert) and assesses performance after supervised fine-tuning (SFT).

stories.title: LACE: Layer-Wise Compression for Dynamic Frame Rate Codecs
stories.author: Shinji Watanabe
bullet_points: The research addresses the high computational cost associated with neural audio codecs due to their high frame rates.
The proposed method, LACE, uses dynamic frame rate codecs to reduce effective frame rates by merging multiple frames.
LACE improves upon prior work by applying compression across multiple quantization layers, unlike methods that use a single compression step.

stories.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
stories.author: Amir Feder
bullet_points: Addresses the difficulty in evaluating social reasoning in LLM assistants due to subjective user narratives and lack of ground truth for social properties.
Introduces 'Fuse,' a multi-agent simulation framework designed specifically for studying user-mediated social reasoning.
Focuses on improving the robustness and verifiability of LLM assistants when providing social advice.

stories.title: Enhancing Accessibility of Medical Texts through Large Language Model-Driven Plain Language Adaptation
stories.author: Hsin-Hsi Chen
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically simplify complex medical texts into plain language.
This addresses a critical healthcare accessibility gap, improving patient comprehension of technical medical information.
The work leverages LLMs (like GPT and BART) for Plain Language Adaptation (PLA), particularly in low-data scenarios (zero-shot/few-shot learning).

stories.title: Forgery of C2PA on a Pixel 10
stories.author: hackerfactor.com via lvig
bullet_points: The news concerns a vulnerability or exploit related to C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) on a Pixel 10 device.
The title suggests a 'forgery' attack targeting the digital provenance standard.
This indicates potential security risks in content authentication mechanisms on high-end Android hardware.

stories.title: Build real-time voice applications with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe
stories.author: thorwebdev
bullet_points: Google has released new Gemini Live models within the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
These new models specifically enable the building of real-time voice applications.
The update leverages Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe capabilities.
